messages.content: Write an internal proposal asking leadership for a quarter of engineering time to pay down technical debt. Around 250 words.

output:
**Subject: Proposal — Dedicate Q4 Engineering Capacity to Technical Debt**

**The ask:** One quarter of engineering time, spread across the team, to pay down technical debt that's now slowing every roadmap item we ship.

**Why now:** Feature velocity has dropped over the last two quarters even though headcount hasn't changed. Code reviews take longer because the codebase has inconsistent patterns from three different architectural eras. Onboarding a new engineer now takes six weeks instead of two, mostly spent explaining workarounds that exist for reasons nobody remembers. Our incident count is climbing, and a growing share traces back to the same fragile modules — the payments retry logic and the auth session layer, in particular.

We've been treating debt paydown as something to squeeze into the margins of sprints. That hasn't worked. It gets deprioritized every time, and the interest keeps compounding.

**What we'd do with the quarter:**
- Refactor the payments retry logic and auth session layer (the two areas responsible for most recent incidents)
- Consolidate three overlapping internal libraries into one
- Raise test coverage on the checkout flow, our highest-risk, lowest-coverage path
- Delete dead code and unused feature flags — a smaller effort, but it removes a lot of noise for reviewers

**What leadership gets in return:** Faster feature delivery starting in Q1, fewer production incidents, and shorter onboarding time for new hires. We'd also come out with clearer ownership boundaries, which should reduce the cross-team coordination overhead we've been absorbing on nearly every launch.

Happy to walk through specifics or adjust scope if a full quarter isn't feasible.
